priceValidity.FINAL_PRICE_VALIDITY: candidate: a non-finite or non-positive catalogue price is not a valid price; the part contributes 0 and is reported in missingParts so current cost reports incomplete
BEHAVIOR_DELTA: price 0: master accepted silently (hidden zero), candidate reports the part as unpriced
price negative: master produced a NEGATIVE total, candidate contributes 0
price null/undefined/non-numeric: master produced NaN in the detail price and NaN in the total, candidate contributes 0
supplier fallback with a 0 row: master could pick the 0 row as the minimum, candidate reports unpriced
why: a missing or invalid catalogue price already contributed exactly 0 to the total in every case, so no legitimate total changes

negative and NaN totals are not a business outcome the current formal API supports, and currentRecipeCost defines costComplete as missingParts.length === 0, so reporting the part is the correct formal semantic

the accepted N4.1C-R3 requirement is exactly that an incomplete cost must be reported rather than a complete cost that omits an unpriced part; the native preview suite asserts that (tests/recipeScenarioComparison.test.cjs) and passes
the production warning path (frameBuilder, catalogReferenceAudit, costDifference, aiResponsePresenter '已定价' wording) improves consistently rather than regressing
priceValidity.residualRisk: a production catalogue row with price 0 now makes the cost report incomplete where it previously reported complete. That is the intended behaviour and matches the documented '缺少价格' contract, but it is a user-visible change and is recorded as such.
